Before you board

PortalNo single portal: Bahrain NHRA (nhra.bh); Oman and Kuwait via their ministries ↗ (opens in a new tab)

Bahrain: licence-application fee BD 20 plus licensure exam BD 50, then a new licence fee of BD 60, 80 or 100 by grade. Kuwait: KD 20 for government-sector licence issuance. Oman: fee NOT FOUND. Oman and Bahrain need DataFlow credential verification, and all three need an employer sponsor and a work visa.

How this was checked: NHRA Bahrain Decision 17 of 2016 and Kuwait's e.gov.kw MOH service page were checked on 3 Nov 2026; Oman's practitioner fees are NOT FOUND on official pages.

01

What it costs

  • Bahrain: BD 20 application, BD 50 exam, then a licence at BD 60, 80 or 100 by grade.
  • Kuwait: KD 20 licence issuance for the government sector.
  • Oman: fee not published on the official pages we could check. Add credential verification and visa costs.

02

Who can apply

  • Bahrain: usually invited by a licensed facility through NHRA's Mehan system.
  • Oman: an Omani employer sponsor is mandatory, plus an OMSB classification exam via Pearson VUE.
  • Kuwait: employer-driven, with a Ministry of Health interview.

03

Dates that matter

  • No fixed window in any of the three.
  • Realistically you would only be eligible after the internship ends in late 2027.

04

How it fits the US and Europe goals

A Gulf licence is not recognised for US or European practice. A job there could build savings and clinical experience, but it is not US clinical experience, and Gulf contracts can pull you off the 2029 Match timeline. Treat it as a financing option, not a pathway.

05

The catches

  1. 01

    Catch 1: sponsor first

    A licence alone does not give you a job or visa.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: unverified experience rules

    The board's two-to-three-year figures come from secondary sources.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: Oman unknown

    No official fee schedule was found.

  4. 04

    Catch 4: Bahrain fees are old

    The published table dates from a 2016 resolution; confirm in Mehan.

06

The honest recommendation

Not a priority now. Revisit after the internship if you need a paid year; ask an actual employer what they require before spending on verification.

Half loan, last resort, and not for the UK or Russia

The Aga Khan Foundation International Scholarship Programme funds postgraduate study as 50% grant and 50% loan, as a resource of last resort. Bangladesh is eligible. The 2026-27 cycle is closed; the next opens in early 2027, with no closing date published yet.

✦ Drafted by Gemini (an AI), then rewritten and fact-checked against official pages on 2–3 Nov 2026. Where they disagreed, the official page won.

  • Good fitYour interestsMaster's in public health or epidemiology fits.

Before you board

PortalAKDN International Scholarships page (no central portal; apply via local AKF contact) ↗ (opens in a new tab)

There is no central online portal. Use the eligibility tool on the AKDN page to get your local AKF team's details. The page states no application fee. The next cycle opens in early 2027, with no closing date published.

How this was checked: AKDN's official International Scholarships page was checked on 3 Nov 2026; it states the 2026-27 cycle is closed, the next opens early 2027, and no fee or closing date is published (NOT FOUND).

01

What it pays

  • A mix of 50% grant and 50% loan. The loan carries a service charge and starts repaying six months after you finish or withdraw.
  • A guarantor must co-sign the loan.
  • Master's applicants are prioritised; PhD funding covers only the first two years.

02

Who can apply

  • Bangladesh is an eligible country. Preference goes to applicants under 30.
  • You must show real financial need and a multi-source funding plan, and already be admitted to a reputable postgraduate institution, starting year one.
  • Not available for study in the United Kingdom or Russia.

03

Dates that matter

  • 2026-27 cycle: closed.
  • Next cycle: opens early 2027. No closing date is published yet.

04

How it fits the US and Europe goals

A funded MPH could add a research record and a network, but it does not replace Step 1, Step 2 CK or ECFMG certification. Because half the award is a loan, a US master's would still cost far more than your budget, and the UK is excluded.

05

The catches

  1. 01

    Catch 1: loan half

    50% must be repaid with a service charge, and a guarantor signs.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: admission first

    You need an offer before the award, so tuition deposits and application fees come first.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: UK excluded

    Imperial, LSHTM and Edinburgh are not eligible.

  4. 04

    Catch 4: limited awards

    A small number per cycle, with need and a multi-source plan required.

06

The honest recommendation

Low priority. Watch the AKDN page in early 2027, but only apply if you already have a place somewhere outside the UK and a clear way to carry the loan.

Not open to you this cycle: you need USMLE or PLAB 1 first

NZREX is New Zealand's clinical registration exam for doctors who qualify through a prerequisite exam. You need a pass in PLAB Part 1, MCCQE Part I, AMC MCQ or USMLE Steps 1 and 2 CK within the last 5 years, so you cannot sit the 2027 sittings. It is only a backup once your USMLE steps are done.

PortalMCNZ NZREX page: application by email to examinations@mcnz.org.nz ↗ (opens in a new tab)

No online portal. Email forms NZREX1 and NZREX3 as PDFs with a passport photo. The NZD 860.92 application fee is non-refundable; the NZD 4,966.94 exam fee is invoiced at least three months before the sitting. Both include GST, from 1 Jul 2026.

How this was checked: MCNZ's NZREX page and fees list (effective 1 Jul 2026) were checked on 3 Nov 2026.

01

What it costs

  • NZD 860.92 application plus NZD 4,966.94 exam fee, both with GST.
  • Add flights to Auckland, accommodation, English tests and ECFMG's EPIC verification.

02

Who can apply

  • An acceptable primary medical qualification and English-language requirements met.
  • A pass within the last 5 years in one prerequisite exam.
  • Your degree and exam results must be primary-source verified through ECFMG's EPIC (MyIntealth) before you apply.

03

Dates that matter

  • Sittings: 6 Mar 2027 and 4 Sep 2027 in Auckland.
  • No closing date; applications are taken in order and fill well before any date.

04

How it fits the US and Europe goals

If you pass Step 1 and Step 2 CK for the Match, NZREX stays open as a five-year backup. It has no European recognition and no research angle. Passing does not give registration: you still need a first-year training job in New Zealand.

05

The catches

  1. 01

    Catch 1: prerequisite gap

    You have no qualifying exam yet.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: job not guaranteed

    Passing NZREX does not guarantee a PGY1 post; the pass rate averages 66%.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: cost

    Fees alone are about NZD 5,800 before travel.

  4. 04

    Catch 4: five-year clocks

    Both the prerequisite and the NZREX pass expire after 5 years.

06

The honest recommendation

Do not spend on this now. Keep it in mind as a fallback once Step 1 and Step 2 CK are passed, and revisit the fee list then.

What it pays

  • International places: 10 scholarships, 25 Finalist Awards of CAD 20,000 a year for up to 2 years (tenable at McGill) and 15 Regional Awards of CAD 10,000 (any public Canadian university).

02

Who can apply

  • International applicants are 'any other citizenship or nationality' than Canadian. Bangladesh is not named, so eligibility is an inference.
  • For the 2027 cohort: a current student on track for a first bachelor's by Aug 2027, or a first bachelor's within the last five years, or a first bachelor's longer ago and aged 30 or under on 1 Jan 2026.
  • You must also meet McGill's minimum degree and language requirements. PhDs, executive masters, certificates and part-time study are excluded.

Thesis-based and PhD applications go through the Nabegh portal on the KFUPM Graduate Studies site. No application fee or thesis/PhD deadline was found on the official pages.

01

What it pays

  • No tuition, a stipend according to category, free furnished on-campus housing.
  • Air tickets for international students, medical and dental care, subsidised meals and free textbooks.
  • The stipend amount is not published. The notes' SAR figures were not on the official page.

02

Who can apply

  • Applicants with a four-year bachelor's in engineering or science with a major in the proposed field or evidence of suitable background.
  • GPA 3.00 or above for scholarship applicants (2.50 without). IELTS 6.0 for MS, 6.5 for PhD. Two recommendation letters.
  • Open to international applicants (a visa is required). The scholarship is for 'distinguished applicants with high GPA', not every admit.

03

Dates that matter

  • Project-based MS: 10 Feb 2027. That is fee-paying, not the scholarship route.
  • Thesis MS and PhD: no deadline found on the pages checked. The application link on the site is live.
  • The graduate bulletin says applications open twice a year.

04

How it fits the US and Europe goals

  • There is no clinical or public-health programme here, so the degree would not support a residency application and would not license you anywhere. It is only relevant if you want to leave medicine for a technical field.

05

The catches

  1. 01

    Catch 1: field mismatch

    The programmes are engineering, science and business.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: no deadline

    The thesis and PhD date is not published.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: stipend unknown

    The notes' SAR 1,725 and 2,400 are not official; the student handbook mentions a different figure of SAR 890, period unclear.

  4. 04

    Catch 4: merit-based

    Not every admitted student gets the scholarship.

06

The honest recommendation

  • Skip it for your plan. It matters only if you decide on a non-medical engineering or science graduate degree.
